Live · Admin (Adam only)

STA Support Expert

Internal diagnostic reference for School Tech product troubleshooting - the heavier-context counterpart to the staff-shared STA Support Chat.

What it is

A Cowork assistant Adam uses to troubleshoot School Technology product issues at depth. It explains causes and fixes grounded in the STA Help Center, drafts customer-facing replies, and answers Skyward navigation questions with cited click-paths. At v2.0 it absorbed the former Skyward Advisor, taking over its platform-detection and coverage-routing capability.

What it does

  • Diagnoses product issues across the full line - time clocks, tardy kiosk, SchoolTRAK, positive attendance, food service, visitor management, ID badging, transcript labels - from 19 context files covering products, how-tos, and product mechanics.
  • Explains Help Center-grounded causes and fixes, citing the underlying article rather than guessing.
  • Drafts customer-facing replies ready for Adam to review and send.
  • Answers Skyward navigation questions with cited click-paths, including platform detection (PaC vs Qmlativ).
  • Covers the support-adjacent stack too: remote access tools (SSH, VNC, WinSCP) and the SQL Server ecosystem (ODBC, SQL Express, SSMS).
Hard rule - grounded answers only. Causes and fixes trace to Help Center content or product context files. Skyward navigation answers carry cited click-paths, not from-memory guesses.

What it does not do

  • Staff-shared support Q&A → that is STA Support Chat (the team-facing Claude.ai Project).
  • Time clock log-file analysis → the Time Clock Error Log Review skill handles uploaded logs.
  • Help Center content strategy and gap audits → Help Center Advisor.

How to access it

Lives in Adam's Cowork workspace. Cowork-only; not shared with staff.

Try starting with

"A district says punches stopped syncing from their TT7s - walk me through likely causes."

"Draft a reply to this customer email about a tardy kiosk that won't print passes."

"Where in Qmlativ does the attendance import mapping live? Give me the click-path."
